title: Operationalized Prompt Templates — scratchpad
content:
Notes to self / half-PRD: operationalized prompt templates (OTP).

Why: we keep shipping endpoint-level prompt wiring in app code (and a dozen ad-hoc YAML files) and it slows iteration, leaks product logic, and makes A/Bing + observability painful. Need a lightweight path to treat prompts as first-class, versioned, validated artifacts that are easy for app teams to consume via the API and Redwood Console.

Goals (high level):
- Make prompts discoverable and versioned in Redwood Console and via API.
- Provide runtime features: templating variables, conditional blocks, strict/lenient validation modes, and simple canary rollouts for prompt changes.
- Surface prompt-level telemetry (token cost per template, median latency, quality signal hooks).
- Keep infra surface small: store templates as small JSON/YAML blobs, immutable versions, lightweight validation, and use existing model routing policies.

Primary personas:
- Product engineer integrating a prompt-driven feature (PLG product teams).
- ML engineer / prompt engineer who iterates on prompt wording and evals.
- Support/analytics person who needs to track regressions tied to prompt changes.

User stories (examples):
- As a product engineer, I can reference a prompt template by id and version in my API call so I don't embed prompt text in application code.
- As a prompt engineer, I can create a draft, run preview tests, and promote to a versioned template with release notes and a canary percentage.
- As an ops person, I can see cost breakdown by template for the last 7/30 days and flag templates exceeding budget triggers.

Core components (sketch):
- Template store: small metadata + body. Fields: id, name, description, author, created_at, versions[]. Each version: version_id, content, bindings (list of expected variables + types), validation_mode (strict|lenient), rollout (0-100%), notes, created_by.
- API: POST /prompt-templates (create draft), GET /prompt-templates/{id}, GET /prompt-templates/{id}/versions, POST /prompt-templates/{id}/promote, PATCH /prompt-templates/{id}/rollout.
- Runtime: when a request references template_id (and optional version), the runtime resolves text, injects bindings from request, runs a short validation pass (size, placeholder coverage), and returns diagnostics if errors in strict mode. Canary: runtime samples based on rollout percent and uses fallback to pinned template if new version not available.
- Console: list, preview, test harness (send sample input, view tokens + model output), diff between versions, metrics panel for cost/latency/quality hooks.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- Create/edit/publish a template via API and Console (draft -> publish).
- Templates can be referenced in generation calls by id/version and expand with bindings correctly.
- Version promotion supports canary rollout (10/100) and runtime obeys rollout config.
- Template-level telemetry ingested and visible in console for 7d.
- Basic validation rejects missing required bindings when used in strict mode.

Metrics to track (initial):
- Templates created per week.
- % of generation calls referencing templates vs inline prompt text.
- Token delta per template version change (tokens before/after).
- % of template-related failures (validation or expansion errors).
- Canary fail rate + rollback frequency.

Open questions / tradeoffs:
- Storage model: small DB row per template vs store in object store (S3) and index in DB. S3 easier for big multi-line templates and diffs; DB simpler for atomic updates and search.
- Validation complexity: how far do we go? Placeholder coverage + simple regex type checks vs embedding-based semantic checks. MVP: simple checks only.
- Exposure surface: do we permit templates to contain function/tool-call scaffolding or should that be separate? Potential security considerations.
- Rollout granularity: user-level, tenant-level, or global percent? MVP: global percent per template version.
- Permissions model: who can publish; we need RBAC for orgs.

Potential implementation timeline (very rough):
- Week 0-2: prototype data model + minimal API for create/get; console list view.
- Week 3-4: preview harness (run against hosted model), binding expansion, basic validation.
- Week 5-6: versioning + promote + canary runtime sampling.
- Week 7-8: telemetry plumbing + console metrics.

Risk & mitigation:
- Risk: Prompt changes cause quality regressions in customer apps. Mitigation: require release notes, optional gated canaries, and tie to eval harness so PE can run a small prompt test suite before promote.
- Risk: Templates allow secrets leakage (e.g., embedding auth tokens). Mitigation: add validator that rejects typical secret patterns and document best practices.

Nice-to-haves (post-MVP):
- Template libraries / marketplace (shared community templates).
- Wrap templates with pre/post hooks that run small transforms (e.g., normalize dates).
- A/B by routing policy (route traffic by user segment).
- Integration with Optimize: suggest quantization or model variant per template based on token profile.

Notes / Todo (personal):
- Talk to Maya to figure out preview harness UX and existing eval harness hooks. (slack @maya)
- File an infra spike ticket for storage model (RDW-4900).
- Sketch console wires focused on diff view and rollout modal.
- Check with security about templates containing inline function calls (cc: security-team).

Inbox thoughts (brain dump):
- Could we auto-suggest variable bindings using a quick ML heuristic on template text? e.g., detect {{user_name}} and suggest type string/email/date. Low-risk: UX suggestion only.
- For big clients, provide an import tool (CSV/YAML) to bulk migrate existing prompt files.
- Consider a "pinned stable" flag for templates where apps can opt-in to guaranteed reproducibility (no auto-promote).

References / similar ideas I saw in drive: prompt-unit-test-harness notes, reusable-instruction-libraries brainlet — overlap but OTP is more ops-focused (versioning + rollout + telemetry).

Next steps (this week):
- Quick huddle with Maya + Leo to validate MVP scope (30m).
- Draft three console screens (list, preview/test, promote modal) and drop into design sync.
- Create RDW-4900 (spike) and RDW-4901 (API skeleton) tickets.

-- Priyanka
(early-stage, personal scratchpad; not yet shared more widely)
